---
title: "Advice or Enforcement"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Guard the Door. **Objective:** sort every control on this site by whether it advises, asks or enforces, and choose the right one for each risk.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude Code docs and OpenCode V2 docs on 2026-11-16 (sources in `research/tools-and-guards.md`)</span>
:::

Every control you have met does one of three things.

- **Advises.** It puts words in front of the model: an instructions file, Skill text, a line in your prompt. The model reads it and may weigh it against everything else in its context. Nothing stops a tool call.
- **Asks.** The harness pauses and puts the decision to you: a permission prompt, or an `ask` rule. It is only as good as your attention at the tenth prompt of the hour.
- **Enforces.** Code outside the model refuses the action whatever the model wants: a `deny` rule, a hook that exits 2 (exit code 2 is how a hook says block), a sandbox (an operating-system layer that limits what commands can touch) where one is on. Enforcement has edges too, listed below.

The Gatehouse's rule of thumb: advice for preferences, a prompt for decisions you want to make each time, enforcement for things that must never happen.

## Each control, and its edge

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

| Control | Kind | Edge, per the docs read or earlier quests |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md`, Skill text, your prompt | Advises | Influences the model only. |
| Permission prompt or `ask` rule | Asks | You must read it. A project `.mcp.json` server has its own approval prompt, and `-p` runs (non-interactive, headless) cannot show it. |
| `deny` rule | Enforces | Matching on command arguments is fragile (see the Carapace quest). Deny and ask rules are still evaluated when a hook returns allow. |
| `PreToolUse` hook, exit 2 | Enforces | Fires only on tool calls, sees the literal text, fails open if it crashes. |
| Sandbox | Enforces | Off by default, and limits shell commands only (see the Carapace quest). The docs say its restrictions still apply if a prompt injection bypasses the model's decision. |
| Git history | Recovers | Recovery only, with no prevention: a commit is a restore point that exists whatever the model did next. |

A hook that **exits 0 with no JSON decision adds no control**: it expresses no decision and the normal permission flow runs. (A hook can also exit 0 and print a JSON `deny` decision, which does block.)

## OpenCode + Ollama

| Control | Kind | Edge, per the V2 docs read |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions file, Skill text, your prompt | Advises | Influences the model only. |
| Permission rule with effect `ask`; no matching rule | Asks | No match means `ask`. |
| Permission rule with effect `deny` | Enforces | An explicit configured `deny` is final and does not invoke the hook. |
| Plugin permission hook (`evaluate`) | Enforces when it denies | Runs for `allow` and `ask` decisions, and can change the effect to `deny`. |
| Git history | Recovers | Recovery only; it prevents nothing. |

Not checked for OpenCode: an exit-code-2 equivalent, whether throwing in a tool hook blocks a call, sandboxing, and the effect of a local Ollama model. Check the current docs before counting on any of them.

:::

## Choose by the cost of being wrong

| Risk | Control | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Style: prefer `snake_case`, tidy commit messages | Advice | A miss costs a review comment. |
| Pushing to a shared branch | Ask | You want to decide each time, with context. |
| Reading `.env` or key files | Deny rule on the Read tool, plus sandbox or hook for Bash (enforce); still not total | It must never happen, so use enforcement, and cover each route the agent could use. |
| A specific destructive command you can name | Blocking hook (enforce) | Code refuses it. It covers only what it matches. |
| Fetched text telling the agent to act | Least privilege, read-only servers, sceptical reading | Advice may not hold against text the model has already read, so limit what the agent can do. |
| An experiment that might wreck your files | Git commit plus a scratch folder | Recovery only; it prevents nothing. |

Layer them: advice to steer, enforcement for the non-negotiable, git for the day something slips through. None of them replaces reading the diff.

The AI for Science best practices (a European draft with no endorsements yet) make the same split for research groups and add a few habits. Put limits in the system that runs the agent: permission scopes, and spend caps in the metering system, because a budget the agent can exceed is not a limit. Give each agent duty a named human owner. Log what an agent did under an identity you can trace. Keep a list of the agents in use, including personal ones connected to mail or files. Their example is an agent with shell access on a shared server, under an account that could see every group's directory, that deleted another group's data; the fixes are a scoped account, a backup before write access, and a named owner for the machine. Last verified (docs, not run): the practice page, read 2026-11-20 via a fetch summary; see `research/aiforscience.md`.

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Best practices for Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it describes instructions as context and not as enforced configuration, which is this quest's core split.
- [AI for Science, practice 4: govern autonomy and accountability](https://aiforscience.eu/best-practices/04-govern-autonomy-and-accountability/): AI for Science (European draft best practices), docs. Why read: it puts limits in the system, names an owner for each agent duty and keeps an inventory. A draft; the page flags some of its own source attributions as unverified.
- [Configure permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it explains deny, ask and allow rules and permission modes, the built-in enforcement layer.
- [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it documents how a hook blocks a tool call, the code-level lock.
- [Configure the sandboxed Bash tool](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it shows an operating-system limit on shell commands and where that limit ends.
:::
